questions.question: Which address belongs to the RFC 1918 block beginning with 10?

option_explanations.A: 100.64.0.0/10 is shared carrier address space, outside RFC 1918.
option_explanations.C: An address starting with 11 is outside 10.0.0.0/8.

questions.question: A branch is selecting a private 192.x address for a lab host. Which candidate falls within RFC 1918 space?

option_explanations.B: The private 192.x block fixes the second octet at 168.

questions.question: Which supplied router interface address falls inside the 172.16.0.0/12 private block?
questions.explanation: A /12 here covers second octets 16 through 31.

option_explanations.A: The private second-octet range ends at 31.
option_explanations.B: 63 is above the private second-octet range.
option_explanations.C: 15 is below the private range starting at 16.
option_explanations.D: A /12 here covers second octets 16 through 31.

questions.question: Which allocation is completely within RFC 1918 space?
questions.explanation: 172.24.0.0/13 covers 172.24 through 172.31. The other options extend outside the private ranges.

option_explanations.A: 172.24.0.0/13 covers 172.24 through 172.31. The other options extend outside the private ranges.
option_explanations.D: Second octets 0–15 are outside the private 172.16–31 range.

questions.question: Why can two disconnected labs both use 10.40.0.0/16?

options.A: No shared forwarding domain must distinguish the duplicated destinations
options.B: The prefix is unique when both sites use /16
options.C: Every private host address is globally registered twice
options.D: ARP assigns a different IPv4 prefix to each lab

questions.explanation: Private addresses can be reused in isolated networks. Connecting overlapping networks requires a way to disambiguate them.

option_explanations.A: Private addresses can be reused in isolated networks. Connecting overlapping networks requires a way to disambiguate them.
option_explanations.B: Using the same mask preserves the overlap rather than creating uniqueness.
option_explanations.C: Private addressing does not require registration.
option_explanations.D: ARP resolves addresses to local link-layer destinations, not to newly assigned prefixes.

questions.question: A private host browses the public Internet through source NAT. What address is modified on the outbound flow?

options.A: The address in the subnet mask
options.D: The local gateway's configured IPv4 address

questions.explanation: Source NAT presents a translated source address to the outside network.

option_explanations.A: A subnet mask is not a translated address in the IP header.
option_explanations.B: Source NAT changes the originating address. The external destination stays the same.
option_explanations.C: Source NAT presents a translated source address to the outside network.
option_explanations.D: The interface configuration does not change when NAT translates individual packets.

questions.question: An edge router maintains a dynamic translation for an outbound session. How is a returning packet delivered?

options.A: The outside server rewrites the destination to the private address
options.B: The router uses translation state to restore the internal destination
options.C: The inside gateway advertises the private subnet to the Internet
options.D: The inside client assigns the public address to its own NIC

questions.explanation: The NAT device reverses the mapping on the inbound return packet.

option_explanations.A: The outside server replies to the address it saw, which is the translated address.
option_explanations.B: The NAT device reverses the mapping on the inbound return packet.
option_explanations.C: Return delivery relies on NAT state, not a public advertisement of a private prefix.
option_explanations.D: The inside client keeps its private address while the edge presents the translated address.

questions.question: Two offices use different private subnets and have a private WAN with valid routes in both directions. What is required solely because the IPs are private?

options.A: The addresses must be replaced with public loopbacks
options.B: Both routers must use source NAT
options.C: Each office must apply destination NAT to its LAN
options.D: No translation is required for this internal communication

questions.explanation: RFC 1918 addresses can be routed across private networks with coordinated addressing.

option_explanations.A: Public addressing is optional for a private, routed path.
option_explanations.B: Source NAT is not required when the private networks can route to one another.
option_explanations.C: Destination NAT is unnecessary when each destination already has a unique reachable address.
option_explanations.D: RFC 1918 addresses can be routed across private networks with coordinated addressing.

questions.question: Two offices merge and both have a server at 10.50.4.40. Why is adding one route to 10.50.4.0/24 insufficient to address both servers independently?

options.A: A /24 route only accepts broadcast destinations
options.B: The same destination cannot uniquely identify the intended server
options.C: The common mask prevents ARP from resolving any address
options.D: Private prefixes cannot appear in routing tables

questions.explanation: The identical destination is ambiguous in one routing context. Renumbering or appropriate translation can resolve that ambiguity.

option_explanations.A: A /24 route can cover unicast addresses as well as the subnet broadcast.
option_explanations.B: The identical destination is ambiguous in one routing context. Renumbering or appropriate translation can resolve that ambiguity.
option_explanations.C: ARP resolves local IP-to-MAC mappings. It does not disambiguate identical routed IP destinations at different sites.
option_explanations.D: Private prefixes are valid in private routing tables.

questions.question: A firewall log outside the edge sees source 198.51.100.7, while the paired internal capture shows source 10.1.2.7 to the same external destination. Which interpretation matches the evidence and the configured source NAT?

options.A: The edge replaces destination IPs to select its upstream gateway
options.B: The clients changed subnets after the firewall logged them
options.C: The edge presents a different source on its outside path
options.D: The external server rewrites its own destination before the internal capture

questions.explanation: The source changes across the edge. The external destination stays the same.

option_explanations.A: The observed difference is in the source. A gateway is selected by routing decisions.
option_explanations.B: The paired captures show the same flow, with configured NAT accounting for the source change.
option_explanations.C: The source changes across the edge. The external destination stays the same.
option_explanations.D: The evidence is about the outbound source, not an externally rewritten destination.
